function: Jointly learns BS multibeamforming weights and movable-antenna positions (CNN block, two feedforward blocks) maximizing the minimum desired-user beamforming gain under an interference-leakage limit (p. 3, 8)
system: Near-field XL-MIMO LoS, BS with 256 movable antennas, 4 desired and 4 undesired single-antenna users, 1 THz carrier; no RIS (p. 3, 11)
method: NMAP-Net: CNN block plus two feedforward blocks, trained unsupervised with an adaptive loss and stochastic gradient ascent, retrained per realization; Gaussian randomization at inference (p. 3, 9, 11)
data_channel: Custom LoS near-field array response (Eq. 1); random user angles and distances; 2e4 training, 1e4 validation, 1e4 test samples by small perturbations (p. 3, 11)
test_conditions: Per realization, trained on 2e4 samples slightly perturbed around its user locations; tested on 1e4 samples from the same perturbation; averaged over 100 realizations (p. 11)
baselines: Non-learned: SDR upper bound, SCA optimization [29], SDR with random or fixed antenna positions. Learned: DL beamformer of [22], DL models I-II (variants of [31]) (p. 12-14)
metrics: Minimum beamforming gain of desired users (versus N, K, L, D, interference threshold), maximum interference leakage, their CCDF/CDF, learning curves (p. 11-14)
complexity: Inference order O((K+L)N^2 + TN) for the proposed NMAP-Net, compared in Table II with SDP bound O((N^2+K+L)^3.5), SCA, and existing DL models; no runtime (p. 15-16)
q1_support: p. 3: "we consider the line-of-sight (LoS) scenario"; p. 11: "are generated randomly from the uniform" distribution; custom analytic near-field array response, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 11: "In each realization, we train the proposed NMAP-Net according to" Algorithm 1; p. 11: "test samples drawn from (29)", the same perturbation as training; no model is tested in a new condition.
q3_support: p. 13: "the successive convex approximation (SCA) as in [29]" and the SDR bound (p. 12) are non-learned; p. 13: "vector w is optimized via the DL technique in [22]" is the learned baseline; metric is minimum beamforming gain (Figs. 6-10).
q4_support: p. 16: "Therefore, the computational complexity of the proposed NMAP-Net is estimated as" O((K+L)N^2 + TN); Table II (p. 15) compares it with the other schemes.
q5_support: p. 11: "training samples drawn by perturbing slightly the values"; the data are synthetic and generated by the author, and the paper gives no link, DOI, or release statement for code or data, and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included, area 3: the learned model outputs the BS beamformer weights jointly with movable-antenna positions (p. 8); the positions are a physical-layer configuration tied to the beamformer, not antenna hardware design, so the reviewer may confirm. Training is label-free with an adaptive loss (p. 9). The network is retrained in each realization (p. 11), so the sweeps over N, K, L, D, and Ith (Figs. 6-10, p. 12-13) do not test one trained model in new conditions. Existing DL models I-II (Fig. 11, p. 14) are variants of the earlier model [31] and of the proposed architecture, so q3 rests on baseline V [22] and the non-learned SCA and SDR schemes. Page numbers count PDF pages.
